correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the holomorphic derivative at inputs with w≠0 and B≠0. The distinct-root identity gives ∑_{j≠i}(z_i−z_j)^{-1}=(n−1)/(2z_i), so D_i=B/(2z_i) and the stated one-step image holds, including the zero-scale image now explicitly excluded from further pairwise-distinct iteration. The j≠i derivative is −4(t−1)^2/[B^2(1−ζ^{j−i})^2], and rotation with cyclic reindexing gives the constant diagonal. The Fourier-sum increments follow from T_1=−(n−1)/2 and T_{k+1}−T_k=1 on the indicated range, hence S_k−S_1=(k−1)(n+1−k)/2. Evaluating the scaling-mode derivative by the quotient rule and adding this Fourier difference gives the full spectrum. The mode constants are positive with maximum n²−1, and their transverse maximum is (n−1)². At t=r^n>0, (n−1)|t−1|<B, so purely transverse perturbations always contract. Comparing √(n²−1)|t−1| with B gives τ_n on t<1; for t≥1 the norm is bounded by (n−1)/(n+1). The exact factorization of Φ(r)−1 into (r−1)^3 times a positive polynomial divided by B follows by multiplying the three-term power difference and comparing coefficients; together with the sign of Φ(r)−r it proves no overshoot, positive monotone convergence, and the unique positive fixed point. At the correctly ordered root vector the derivative is zero and the map holomorphic, so a small contracting neighborhood exists; pulling it back along each finite radial orbit proves the open-basin assertion.

value.rationale: Regular polygons are natural equally spaced starts for the binomial. The exact ambient decomposition identifies both the maximum one-step amplification and the unexpected fact that transverse modes strictly contract even in the scaling-mode expansion regime; it therefore separates perturbation mechanisms rather than just giving a scalar convergence rate. The result is a sharp idealized algorithm benchmark, not a claim that pure transverse perturbations expand or that nearby starts diverge.
